reviews.review_msg: I think Andrew is an amazing instructor, he did great work. He made the course very interesting and engaging. I have learned lots from it! I appreciate him explaining the ideas with concrete examples and also his own perspectives. I am an extremely emulative person, and his thoughts were a significant path for me in the future!
Andrew recorded awesome lectures! He and the TA gave me helpful feedback on my assignments. Really enjoyed the course. Be prepared to write tho
very unclear instructions, the way he and TA marked did not follow the instructions.

One of the coolest prof I ever had lol. I'm graduating next semester and regret that I did not take his classes sooner. Will definitely re-take his class if I have a chance. Funny and caring with examples that get us through a dry writing class. If you like Stephen Zilwood, you will definitely like his teaching style.

I've had Rahman for a few classes and I think he's a great professor. Easy going and if you show a genuine interest in his subject material he will want you to succeed. Has a lot of reading required, so prepare for that. Overall he tries his best to make the class interesting so if you show face that is what matters.

One of the most caring professors at SFU. He's very knowledgeable about international affairs. I've taken 3 courses with him and always enjoyed informative lectures and got rewarded for my participation in class. He seemed to struggle with assignment guideline in this course, perhaps bcz he tried to incorporate too many suggestions from students

Brutal lectures. He overloads students with WAY more examples than needed, way past the point when everyone understands the concept. Not good with technology, wastes a lot of time trying to get videos to load. Assignment guidelines unclear and disorganized.

Dr. Hauck knows what he's talking about, that's for sure. However, I don't think his specialities were highlighted in the format of an online class. Only copied and pasted text from the readings in his slides, which made it really difficult to stay engaged. Tons of readings and homework. Take another W class if you have to.

Important Notes: 
- If you can, do NOT take this class (or any) at 8:30 AM.
- Passionate prof and entertaining lectures
- Heavy on theory and lots of readings, but he explains them well. Do not skip, as it's hard to grasp content on your own. 
- Pop quizzes on readings
- Grading can be difficult ngl
- Prof is genuine, understanding, and empathetic

He's a funny & friendly guy who is clearly passionate about the topic, but he seems to have a very philosophical approach to communications which made things a bit more confusing than they needed to be. Lectures were boring in my opinion, but the assignments were really easy. Lots of readings too but you can follow along fine w/o them
Honestly, one of the best profs in SFU CMNS, everyone should take this course with him.
Grading criteria was super unclear even though I asked a ton of questions. TA wasn't helpful at all. Lectures weren't super interesting. Would avoid this prof.

For a sessional lecturer he's hands down one of the best teachers in the whole program. The way he engages with student participation and questions beats a lot of profs in the program and it's really clear he deserves a bigger role. enjoyed the course and others shared the same opinion, enjoy the philosophy edge he brings.
Good prof. Lectures can be sorta hard to follow but he gets really into them.
A very nice professor! Would take his course again!
This TA actually cares. What a shock! Discussions get kind of off topic sometimes and also a hard marker!

I disagree with the other one. Clayton was totally helpful TA, very approachable and  friendly with students, edgy sense of humour and funny stories. He pushes your boundaries and challenges you to think. I went to him several times for help with my assignments, essays he was always helpful. I wish I could say the same for the prof. This course suc
good TA...knowledgable and interesting....but not very approachable or friendly
Very knowledgeable but hard to stay focused because his voice is really monotone.

The lectures for this course is super fun but when you have to sit down and write your own paper, most likely, you'll be stuck and become irritated. Although Gary is delighted prof, his TA was unhelpful and unclear..think before you take this course!!!!
A very interesting lecturer, with soem lectures actually being applicable to everyday life. Amazing stuff.
GREAT GUY!!  Very smart, entertaining and challenging...

An excellent teacher who's always willing to help the students out.  ** If you get the chance to take a class with him, DO NOT pass it up! **  He's super intelligent and a genuinely good guy.  Great lectures - lots of humor and insight.
Great Prof., Great elaboration.
articulate, funny, sincere

She's a TA for cmns 304 and was terrible at providing any helpful feedback to improve in the course. She doesn't explain things very well. Expects students to do all the work in the class. Would not recommend. Difficult marker and provides no justification :(

For CMNS315: She babies her students and changed the course structure over a month into the semester—after the withdrawal deadline. This suddenly forced attendance for the three-hour weekly lectures. She also banned electronics in class even for note taking. It feels like elementary school. 

Just take another class cause its not worth it!

This is for CMNS 315 and not 304. The prof is so disorganised, the layout of the class kept changing every week. The weekly participation was initially online, then it was in class on paper at the beginning of lecture and the following week it was at the end of the lecture. Lectures are not engaging at all. Would not recommend.

Easily the worst instructor. She's lazy and unprepared and doesn't even lecture, she just pads time by asking vague questions that the same 2 students answer over and over. She's antagonistic towards students, doesn't share lecture slides with us, she didn't even bother to show us the grading rubric for assignments before we submitted them. Avoid!

She is a caring professor but extremely authoritative. She loses her mind if you even glance at your phone in class and is very judgy with people who might be struggling in her class. Not supper accommodating, judgemental, authoritative, controlling, and rude.
Hot as hell. I have no idea what this class was about.

has bad breathe which is likely because he is genetically recessive. stuffy and overly philosophical for a course on everyday life. I must admit though that he really is a complete sex bomb. God help us if he becomes a prof.
Will miss his grandiosity
Is purely interested in philosophy.

Scott was by far one of the worst TA's I have ever had. Given that this class title is communication in everday life, Scott seems to overlook that and focuses more on making life and class impossible to complete. He is extremely arrogant and very difficult to approach. Personally I have never met a worse TA. Communication becomes flawed bc of him.

I've had tough TAs but it was always in "tough love." This guy goes out of his way to make life difficult (see below comments.) Half my tutorial switched or dropped. If you decide to tough it out and Scot goes too far, email the professor. It was only then that Scot stopped kicking people out and the proposal was changed back to 2 pages.

Horrible person. Kicked people out the first class for being even 2 min. late. Rude, mean, unreachable expectations. Having him as a teacher is a big regret.  I hope karma makes him suffer the way we have to suffer with him. I don't know how I will be able to get through this class.  Horrible person.

The first rating is totally bogus. Scott is mean, aggressive, uses unprofessional language, lies about assignment expectations (says a proposal is 8-10 pages when it's really only 2), kicks people out of class if they show up 5 min. late, and constantly interrupts the tutorial to chastise the late student. Hard marker, readings mandatory, scary guy
No Comments

He is a great TA who helps his students and stuff. Super easy going guy, really friendly, and nice. He totally grades easy, so if your into an easy A TAKE HIS CLASS. I like, did no readings a nd got an A+. LOVE HIM!

Very dissapointed in a professor who uses a 3rd-year lecture as her personal soap-box.  If you don't agree with her extreme-left ideologies and feminist rhetoric then don't bother. Her shock value goes beyond keeping students interested and crosses into the realm of distraction.  Good-luck focusing on the actual course content!

Worst class i've ever taken.  Silva obviously hated our class, and she did not make any point of trying to hide it.  She was not approachable, or friendly, or willing to help.  She was annoyed with the amount of emails she received, and she made you feel stupid if you didn't agree with her. Bah!

interesting and thought provoking lectures...guys might not like it...she's an obvious feminist and her lectures do demonstate this...but its about time for a strong opinionated female professor to come around...

very biased. does not give room for creativity or self-expression. how can anyone like this teach? total propaganda and brainwashing. i don't think there is a need to be referring to homosexuality during evey lecture.

lecture topics are interesting but what is really annoying and frustrating is how she presents the material in class, her personal biasness makes the stuff she talks about less appealing... Avoid her if you don't want lectures in the feminist perspective!
she's very knowledgeable, but like what the person before me posted, sort of like her way or the highway.
I *so* regret taking this class! It is so dry & boring and Silva's personal biasness gets in the way. It's her opinion or the highway.

Steven is so passionate in his lectures. He has a tendency to be a bit all over the place but you learn so much if you pay attention and get involved. His office hours are also super helpful and he'll stay so late after lecture to help out his students. He really cares about all of his students and wants them to do well in his class!
never take this course with him! He is confusing and also a tough grader. His TA doesn't look like they want to teach the tutorial. Didn't learn anything from this course.
worst professor ever. Only reads from the PPT and a very tough grader.

Steven Malcic was a decent prof. All assignments are graded by the TA so your grade is dependent on whether or not they are a tough grader. Steven is a bit weird and has a strange approach to teaching. This was a writing heavy course so I don't recommend it if it's not mandatory for you.
Class is lecture heavy. Personally, I found it difficult to connect the lectures to the course readings. Speaks awfully slow and has stale humor. Assignments and exam are vague.

Terry was awesome. Really caring, fair, gave good feedback, and was entertaining. I personally really liked the lecture style, but it's definitely different. You'll want to do the readings and participate. As long as you do you'll do well.

Terry is funny and inspiring. His lecture-style can be a little bit eccentric, but I thought that was appropriate given how the entire course is based on the premise of getting you to think outside the box. I'd take Terry any day over a standard, read-off-the-powerpoint professor.

Terry is a nice guy and he is willing to take a look at paper drafts and tell you where you can improve.  That said, I couldn't really follow his lecture style as he presented a new, unrelated topic each week (medical discourse, religious discourse, etc) which was very different than what I expected from the course title.

He's bit eccentric, and his outside-the-box approach to the course left a few people scratching their heads (but those people could use a little shaking up.)  Academia needs more people like this who aren't just spewing the standard fare to be repeated back to them on exams. If you can get over his slight creepy uncle vibe, you'll be glad you came.

Terry was just OK in my opinion. He seems like a genuinely really nice guy who is unquestionably passionate about what he teaches, but I honestly found the whole concept of the course a bit of a stretch. Most of the time I felt like he was just making stuff up. I ended up with a good grade but can confidently say that I have no idea what I learned.

Terry is a great prof, who appears knowledgeable and passionate about the content he teaches. Assignments are fair, and the in-class essay was an open-book test. Overall an interesting class and I enjoyed the lectures.

I do not understand why Terry's mark is so low. He is brillant, funny and interresting. I agree three hours lecture is intense but if you participate and do the readings, you will enjoy his lectures. I intend to take more courses with him, if I can.

This class puzzled me at first, and I felt very lost- but I think I know why. In many CMNS courses, you are expected to regurgitate, and that is what many CMNS students are trained to do. This course's content, however, is very much open to interpretation and you take away your own meaning. I think you should take this class, don't be scared off.
What an amazing instructor. This here is a professor who cares about his students.
Neiman has an interesting background and we're lucky to have him teaching us!

He's such an amazing guy that I would chill with him for fun. Regardless of what grade you get, this is the most genuinely interesting class I've taken at SFU. I'd recommend it for anyone interested in language, dialogue & the human experience.

Couldn't link readings to the lecture without the TAs help. Papers are given without very many guidelines, which makes it hard to know what they're looking for, resulting in lower grades because they mark hard. TA (DYLAN) WAS HORRIBLE WITH PROVIDING FEEDBACK IN A TIMELY FASHION. Get 2 TAs? Can't seem to keep up with the marking. Don't take it.
AWESOME lecturer, had me engaged the whole three hours every time. Brings familiar things like a Hendrix song or an Orson Wells film into context in a way that makes you see things differently.
good
An amazing prof. His lectures were fun and very interesting. This course is definitely worth taking.

One of the most intelligent and genuine profs in CMNS, if you are lucky enough to have him. Terry has had my full attention in every one of our 9AM lectures, and every time, I am compelled to fill my notebook with his words. If you are someone who has a brain and cares for social discourse, you will find this class very intellectually stimulating.

At first I thought I hated Terry because of his dislike of big words. (Seriously, this is an UD CMNS course...) But it turns out I've loved this class. He's a great lecturer & really wants people to learn. You MUST do the readings & keep up with the course. Exams are actually based on learning & understanding, not rote memorisation-what a concept!!
Good prof. Quite difficult but him and TA are willing to help. You learn a lot new concepts in this class.

Terry teaches concepts. You couldn't cheat in this class if you tried. If you are interested in doing graduate school then take a class from Terry.. Encyclopaedic knowledge of Social thinkers/theories from the past 200 years. The most important thing you will learn from Terry is how to make connections from abstractions and relate them to real life

I really like Terry, he is funny and engaging, he does his best to get class participation and he does lots of activities to break the long class up. He is a bit confusing in that it is not always easy to know how what we are talking about relates to the course but if you ask questions he is happy to clarify. He's a cool guy. Course is very different from what I expected, but Terry is a smart guy.

Terry comes off as a great guy. However, his lectures tend to be quite dry most of the time and the readings even drier. For my semester he decided to take attendance in lecture (wasn't a seminar), which really put me off. The class itself is interesting, but the way he presents the material could use a face-lift.

The worst class ever. Instead of list this class as communication course, I think its more like a philosophy class. The course materials are super dry and doesnt make any sense! I cant see how it connects to EVERYDAY LIFE COMMUNICATION. Anyways, do your work you will be fine. I hope someone else can teach this class.

Terry is very passionate and genuine. The course covers a lot of topics that seem unrelated but he brings them all together in a really interesting way. He can be hard to follow sometimes but always is super helpful and willing to clarify. If you engage in the course and pay attention to what he mentions in lectures you'll be golden!
Really intelligent. He is helpful, and makes an effort to make the class interesting and interactive.

Terry is fantastic. He's a great speaker and always makes an effort to make his lectures more interactive. If you're looking to take only one of 323 or 304, I would definitely choose 304, as long as Terry's still teaching it. It's a great primer for a lot of other upper division CMNS courses.
I wish someone else would teach the course :(
Hands down one of the most intelligent profs I have ever come across. This guy just knows stuff about everything and made lectures very enjoyable.

Terry is a wonderful prof and an excellent T/A. He is passionate about what he is teaching and is helpful when students ask questions. This course definitely pushes you to come up with your own ideas and work a little more independently. Topics are not just handed to you on a silver platter. Welcome to upper division courses.

Terry is an awesome. Genuinely nice lecturer and seems to really care in  helping others learn. can't help the fact that the course material is a bit dry overall but it is a 3rd year course. Also, marking is fair but a bit difficult to attain 'excellent' marks.

I was not looking forward to this class from reading comments here, however, after a great semester I absolutely can't understand what everyone's problem is. Terry is a great prof, very dynamic and enthusiastic. He is clear, has good notes but also expects alot from his students - as he should, it's a 3rd yr class! Julie (TA) is awesome too!

I'm surprised at all the bad comments - it's not the most exciting class I've ever taken, that's for sure, but Terry is a nice guy and not a hard marker - good sense of humor too. Rambles a bit in lecture, but if you pay attention and do most of the readings, you're set. Seriously, this class is NOT as difficult as people are making it out to be!!

Terry was one of the best professors I've had at SFU. Some of the other comments on this thread are completely ridiculous; I didn't see half of those things in class! Terry is very fair and has a unique teaching and marking style which I thought was very helpful. He is very nice, clearly interested in the course content, and happy to offer help!

This class has nothing to do with "everyday communication" at all. I am so confused 99% of the time and I honestly never know what the relevance of what he talks about to the course is. Brutal class with so much writing. The readings are so dry as well.

Totally boring and confusing. I tried looking up concepts he talked about and they seem non-existent. Little structure to class. Never missed a class, but not really sure what it was about. Don't take this class! It is nothing like what it sounds like it is about.

Neiman is the worst professor I have encountered so far at SFU. He teaches first year concepts in his 3rd year class, is biased and unhelpful. his textbook is useless, his examples are irrelevant, and his overall attitude towards students is poor. i wish i hadn't taken his class.
Super interesting classes. The class is a bit mind boggling (in a good way). Definitely take it if you like being critical of every aspect of daily life. Great class. Fantastic TA (Angela Gunther).
Don't understand what is trying to get at many of the times...make me have a bad impression of dialogue courses in CMNS. He can be very vague.
Avoid at all cost.The most biased prof I have ever come across. He has a huge ego and loves to hear his own voice.

Neiman is the worst prof anyone could ever have. He loves to hear himself talk while he ignores the concerns of the students. he is not very supportive or attentive during his office hours. kinda makes you feel like you are wasting his time. his class makes no sense and neiman seems to enjoy the fact that his students are all confused.

Terry is an extremely smart guy.  This class is definately not what I thought it would be- "communication in everyday life"... the fairly complex ideas you learn seem like they couldn't be further from everyday life, but they end up making sense.
